problems: None of the chains has a validated regulatory element: E03 and E05 report no cCRE at the variant. The motif evidence is predictive and does not establish regulatory activity.
PELI2 is only a proximity-based candidate. No evidence connects the variant or a regulatory element to PELI2; the low-PIP QTL concerns a different gene, and GTEx reports no significant eQTL.
No chain has supporting breast-cancer association evidence. E27 adds a PELI2–breast-cancer overall score of 0.00; this does not establish a causal link.

The allele direction is consistent across the selected motif predictions: ref C is predicted to bind more. These predictions do not demonstrate allele-specific binding in cells. H4 additionally has no reported ATF7 peak in the matched MCF7 assay; the XBP1 and CREB3L4 lookups report no matching MCF7 assay, not a negative result.

checks.why: A variant-overlapping XBP1 peak in MCF7 would add direct occupancy evidence; a negative result would further weaken the proposed cell-context link.
A variant-overlapping CREB3L4 peak in MCF7 could distinguish this candidate from the other predicted factors.
A breast-cancer association for PELI2 could improve the disease-relevance of this proposed target, although it would not establish a variant-to-PELI2 link.

critique.next_experiment: In MCF7, test allele-specific occupancy at the variant for the leading predicted factors (XBP1 and CREB3L4), with ATF7 as a comparator, and pair any occupancy result with a variant perturbation or reporter assay to test regulatory activity. If activity is observed, follow with a target-gene assay rather than inferring PELI2 from distance.

lookups.why: A variant-overlapping XBP1 peak in MCF7 would add direct occupancy evidence; a negative result would further weaken the proposed cell-context link.
A variant-overlapping CREB3L4 peak in MCF7 could distinguish this candidate from the other predicted factors.
A breast-cancer association for PELI2 could improve the disease-relevance of this proposed target, although it would not establish a variant-to-PELI2 link.

games.reason: Both chains predict stronger in-vitro binding to ref C, and neither has positive variant-overlapping ChIP-seq evidence. A is better supported because the F1 model is specifically XBP1 and XBP1 is highly expressed in MCF7 (636.6 TPM). In B, the best model is CREB3, while CREB3L4 is less highly expressed (48.8 TPM) and the evidence does not resolve CREB3L4 from the similarly expressed CREB3. The not-tested ChIP-seq evidence does not count against either chain.

XBP1 is better supported modestly: its own QBiC-SELEX model predicts a stronger ref-over-alt binding effect than the CREB3L4 model (E13 vs. E14), and XBP1 expression in MCF7 is much higher (636.6 vs. 48.8 TPM). Neither chain has variant-overlapping ChIP-seq support in MCF7, so this comparison rests on the binding predictions and expression context, not demonstrated occupancy.
